claim_boundary: Primary sources support a time-varying relationship between Bitcoin, U.S. monetary conditions and the dollar, but do not establish that a four-week fall in the Federal Reserve broad dollar index predicts BTC or improves DRA economics. Exactly one preregistered matched-capital audit may test the rule; no causal or alpha claim is imported from the literature.

feature_contract.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED
feature_contract.source_agency: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (US)

prior_matrix.identity: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Nominal Broad U.S. Dollar Index via FRED
prior_matrix.finding: The official DTWEXBGS series is a daily nominal broad U.S. dollar index, January 2006 equals 100, not seasonally adjusted, sourced from the Federal Reserve H.10 release and marked public domain with citation requested.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: The present-vintage index is not DXY, not a Bitcoin predictor, and does not identify an exogenous dollar or monetary-policy shock.

prior_matrix.identity: Karau, Monetary policy and Bitcoin, Journal of International Money and Finance 137 (2023)
prior_matrix.finding: Bitcoin's response to U.S. monetary-policy tightening changed over time and since late 2020 became more similar to other risky assets.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: A policy surprise is not a broad-dollar trend state, and the study does not validate this four-week sign rule or DRA admission.

prior_matrix.identity: Regaieg, Moussa and Mgadmi, Can We Reckon Bitcoin as a Hedge, a Safe Haven or a Diversifier for US Dollars?
prior_matrix.finding: The study uses a regime-switching framework to examine Bitcoin and a U.S. Dollar Index and reports regime-dependent hedge or diversification properties.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Its dollar index, sample, regime model and portfolio question differ from DTWEXBGS weekly change, after-cost DRA entries and the 2020-2024 windows.

real_time_design_requirements: Seal exact annual FRED CSV responses for DTWEXBGS from 2018-01-01 through 2024-12-31; require unique weekday dates, positive finite decimal values and no missing marker.
Construct each calendar week ending Friday from all available Monday-Friday observations; require three to five observations and do not interpolate holidays.
Make week-ending Friday D usable only at D plus five calendar days 00:00 UTC and valid for at most 168 hours.
Compare each weekly mean only with the exact weekly mean 28 calendar days earlier; admit the unchanged DRA V1 signal only when the current mean is strictly lower.
Use the frozen 250 USDT DRA V1 parent, 240 USDT slot capacity, 0.10% fee and 0.05% adverse slippage without changing entries, exits, lot size, capacity or accounting.

Require Design, Validation, 2020-2024 annual matched-capital economics, realized/unrealized/total PnL, drawdown, underwater duration, holding, utilization, terminal inventory, intervention breadth, concentration and independent non-overlapping 168-hour predictive diagnostics.

Do not add 1-, 8-, 13-, 26- or 52-week horizons, moving averages, volatility scaling, DXY substitution, inverse rules, magnitude thresholds, rate interactions, fractional sizing, short legs or post-outcome exceptions.
Do not open post-2024 data; a historical pass remains REPORTED_NOT_ACTIVATED and requires separately sealed independent OOS.
uncertainty: Dollar-Bitcoin direction and strength can change across monetary, crisis and crypto-native regimes.
DTWEXBGS is a broad trade-weighted nominal index and differs from the ICE DXY composition commonly used in market commentary.
The present-vintage FRED series can contain revisions; original H.10 release values and revision history remain MISSING_PROOF.
The four-week horizon is a preregistered monthly-scale convention, not a parameter established by the cited papers.
No complete DTWEXBGS history, BTC/DRA outcome, post-2024 observation, candidate, OOS or Trading path was accessed while freezing this prior.
